podcast.body: This song was the band's first hit, breaking into the top 10 on Billboard's Hot 100 at number 10 in the week ending February 18, 1995, after a slow, steady climb. It kicked off a year of mega-stardom for the band. The song was brought to the band by drummer Jim Sonefeld, who was its primary songwriter and whose previous bands had turned it down. To Sonefeld, the song was about "compassion in a cruel world," while Darius Rucker interpreted it as a protest song about "love in the face of hatred," given his experiences with racial epithets in college. For the re-recording on *Cracked Rear View*, Atlantic Records secured David Crosby to provide backing vocals on the chorus. "Whatever it was, Hold My Hand was a rousing sing-along, a hit in the making."
